{{Short description|Blockchain protocol}}
{{About|the protocol|other uses |Ouroboros (disambiguation)}}

[[File:Ouroboros-benzene.svg|thumb|upright=1|The ouroboros, [[August Kekulé|Kekulé]]'s inspiration for the structure of benzene. It is used to symbolize the ever-growing consensus on the Cardano blockchain]]

'''Ouroboros''' is a family of [[Proof of stake|proof-of-stake]] consensus protocols used in the [[Cardano (cryptocurrency platform)|Cardano]] and [[Polkadot (cryptocurrency)|Polkadot]] [[blockchain]]s. It can run both permissionless and permissioned blockchains.<ref>Robby Houben, Alexander Syners (2018) [https://www.europarl.europa.eu/cmsdata/150761/TAX3%20Study%20on%20cryptocurrencies%20and%20blockchain.pdf "Cryptocurrencies and blockchain. Legal context and implications for financial crime, money laundering, and tax evasion"]. July. European Parliament Policy Department for Economic, Scientific, and Quality of Life Policies, Directorate-General for Internal Policies.</ref>

Ouroboros was published as "the first provable secure PoS consensus protocol". It was postulated by an academic team led by [[Aggelos Kiayias]] at the [[International Association for Cryptologic Research#International Cryptology Conference|Annual International Cryptology Conference]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Kiayias |first1=Aggelos |last2=Russell |first2=Alexander |last3=David |first3=Bernardo |last4=Oliynykov |first4=Roman |editor1-last=Katz |editor1-first=J. |editor2-last=Shacham |editor2-first=H. |title=Advances in Cryptology – Crypto 2017 |date=27 July 2017 |publisher=Springer |location=Cham |isbn=978-3-319-63688-7 |pages=357–388 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-63688-7_12 |language=en |chapter=Ouroboros: A Provably Secure Proof-of-Stake Blockchain Protocol|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-63688-7_12 }}</ref> Later that year, Ouroboros (Classic) was implemented by [[IOHK]] as the basis of the Cardano blockchain platform and various upgrades.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hu |first=Charlotte net|title=A beginner's guide to how cryptocurrencies work |url=https://www.popsci.com/technology/beginners-guide-to-cryptocurrency |access-date=2021-12-06 |website=Popular Science |date=15 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Forbes">{{Cite web|last=Ehrlich |first=Steven net|title=Cardano And Ethereum Founder Analyzes The Newest Evolutions In Crypto And Blockchain Technology |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/stevenehrlich/2021/04/26/cardano-and-ethereum-founder-analyzes-the-newest-evolutions-in-crypto-and--blockchain-technology/ |access-date=2021-12-06 |website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=6 May 2020|title=The Blockchain Galaxy A comprehensive research on distributed ledger technologies|url=https://www2.deloitte.com/content/dam/Deloitte/it/Documents/financial-services/Deloitte_Blockchain_galaxy.pdf|access-date=2021-12-07 |website=[[Deloitte]]|quote=}}</ref> Ouroboros versions include:<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ge |first1=Lina |last2=Wang |first2=Jie |last3=Zhang |first3=Guifen |date=2022-05-29 |title=Survey of Consensus Algorithms for Proof of Stake in Blockchain |journal=Security and Communication Networks |language=en |volume=2022 |article-number=e2812526 |doi=10.1155/2022/2812526 |issn=1939-0114|doi-access=free }}</ref>

* Ouroboros BFT was an interim version used in 2020 to enable the switch between the Classic and Praos versions of Cardano using a [[hard fork combinator]]<ref>The Cardano Consensus and Storage Layer (2023) Edsko de Vries,  Thomas Winant and Duncan Coutts. GitHub. https://input-output-hk.github.io/ouroboros-network/pdfs/report/report.pdf</ref> that preserved the blockchain history;<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kiayias |first1=Aggelos |last2=Russell |first2=Alexander |date=30 Oct 2018 |title=Ouroboros-BFT: A Simple Byzantine Fault Tolerant Consensus Protocol |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/1049 |journal=Cryptology ePrint Archive |issue=Report 2018/1049 |access-date=November 23, 2020}}</ref>{{primary source inline|date=November 2020}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Ouroboros BFT |url=https://docs.cardano.org/about-cardano/learn/ouroboros-overview#:~:text=analysis%2E-,Ouroboros%20BFT |access-date=2026-03-09 |website=docs.cardano.org |language=en}}</ref>
* Ouroboros Praos (2017)<ref>{{cite book |last1=David |first1=Bernardo |last2=Gaži |first2=Peter |last3=Kiayias |first3=Aggelos |last4=Russell |first4=Alexander |title=Advances in Cryptology – EUROCRYPT 2018 |chapter=Ouroboros Praos: An Adaptively-Secure, Semi-synchronous Proof-of-Stake Blockchain |date=2018 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-78375-8_3 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |language=en |location=Cham |publisher=Springer |volume=10821 |pages=66–98 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-78375-8_3 |isbn=978-3-319-78374-1|s2cid=4898657 }}</ref> provided security against fully-adaptive corruption in the semi-synchronous model. A team at Cornell University discussed Ouroboros Praos and their own provably secure proof-of-stake protocol called Snow White. In 2020, Praos was used to introduce decentralized block production on Cardano by stake pools;<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Daian |first1=Phil |last2=Pass |first2=Rafael |last3=Shi |first3=Elaine |title=Financial Cryptography and Data Security |chapter=Snow White: Robustly Reconfigurable Consensus and Applications to Provably Secure Proof of Stake |date=2019 |editor-last=Goldberg |editor-first=Ian |editor2-last=Moore |editor2-first=Tyler |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-32101-7_2 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=11598 |language=en |location=Cham |publisher=Springer International Publishing |pages=23–41 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-32101-7_2 |isbn=978-3-030-32101-7|s2cid=34952336 }}</ref>
* Ouroboros Genesis (2018) provides security with a dynamic participation model;
* Ouroboros Chronos (2019) is independent of global time;<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Karpinski |first1=Mikolaj |last2=Kovalchuk |first2=Lyudmila |last3=Kochan |first3=Roman |last4=Oliynykov |first4=Roman |last5=Rodinko |first5=Mariia |last6=Wieclaw |first6=Lukasz |date=2021-09-25 |title=Blockchain Technologies: Probability of Double-Spend Attack on a Proof-of-Stake Consensus |journal=Sensors (Basel, Switzerland) |volume=21 |issue=19 |page=6408 |doi=10.3390/s21196408 |issn=1424-8220 |pmc=8512294 |pmid=34640729|bibcode=2021Senso..21.6408K |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* Ouroboros Crypsinous (2019) gives higher levels of privacy
* Research in 2020 tested Ouroboros Hydra, a protocol version that used "off-chain state channels" (called "heads") to enable peer-to-peer transactions. Such "layer 2" protocols manage transactions off the main blockchain, and each head could potentially process "up to 1,000 transactions per second". In theory, Ouroboros Hydra could rival the 30,000 simultaneous transactions offered by conventional payment systems such as [[Visa Inc.|Visa]] by running scores of heads.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-04-15 |title=Digital Banking Trends Of 2020 |url=https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/digital-banking-trends-of-2020/ |access-date=2023-07-04 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Cardano's founder [[Charles Hoskinson]] has described the Ouroboros consensus mechanism as energy efficient.<ref name="Forbes" /> Nguyen et al. compared Ouroboros to other PoS protocols.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nguyen |first1=Cong T. |last2=Hoang |first2=Dinh Thai |last3=Nguyen |first3=Diep N. |last4=Niyato |first4=Dusit |last5=Nguyen |first5=Huynh Tuong |last6=Dutkiewicz |first6=Eryk |title=Proof-of-Stake Consensus Mechanisms for Future Blockchain Networks: Fundamentals, Applications and Opportunities |journal=IEEE Access |date=2019 |volume=7 |pages=85727–85745 |doi=10.1109/ACCESS.2019.2925010 |s2cid=195883618 |issn=2169-3536|doi-access=free |hdl=10220/49702 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
